subtopics.title: states and capitals
subtopics.teaching: India is a union of states and union territories, and each state has a designated capital for its government.
subtopics.worked_example: Tamil Nadu's capital is Chennai, while Karnataka's capital is Bengaluru.
subtopics.pitfall: A capital is not necessarily the largest or most populous city.
subtopics.mastery: Recall state-capital pairs accurately and distinguish states from union territories.

subtopics.title: national symbols
subtopics.teaching: India has officially recognized national symbols representing national identity and heritage.
subtopics.worked_example: The national animal is the Bengal tiger, the national bird is the Indian peacock, and the national flower is the lotus.
subtopics.pitfall: Popular cultural associations are not automatically official national symbols.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish officially recognized symbols from commonly associated cultural icons.

subtopics.title: constitution basics
subtopics.teaching: The Constitution of India establishes the framework of government, rights, duties and institutional relationships.
subtopics.worked_example: It came into force on 26 January 1950, observed as Republic Day.
subtopics.pitfall: The Constitution is distinct from an ordinary law because it provides the foundational legal framework.
subtopics.mastery: Recall key constitutional features and distinguish them from ordinary administrative facts.

subtopics.title: landmarks
subtopics.teaching: Indian landmarks reflect architectural, historical, religious and cultural heritage.
subtopics.worked_example: The Taj Mahal in Agra is a major Mughal-era monument commissioned by Shah Jahan and associated with Mumtaz Mahal.
subtopics.pitfall: A landmark's city and architectural or historical context should not be confused.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major Indian landmarks, locations and broad significance.

subtopics.title: institutions
subtopics.teaching: India's public institutions have distinct constitutional, legislative, judicial, financial or administrative functions.
subtopics.worked_example: The Supreme Court is the highest court of India, while Parliament is the central legislative institution.
subtopics.pitfall: An institution's popular reputation does not define its formal role.
subtopics.mastery: Match important institutions with their primary functions.

subtopics.title: countries and capitals
subtopics.teaching: Countries have capital cities that serve as important administrative or political centres; the largest city is not always the capital.
subtopics.worked_example: Australia's capital is Canberra rather than Sydney; Brazil's capital is Brasília rather than Rio de Janeiro.
subtopics.pitfall: Assuming the largest city is the capital causes common errors.
subtopics.mastery: Recall country-capital pairs and distinguish capitals from major commercial cities.

subtopics.title: continents and oceans
subtopics.teaching: Continents are large land divisions and oceans are major bodies of salt water.
subtopics.worked_example: In the seven-continent model, Asia, Africa and Europe are separate continents; the Pacific is the largest ocean.
subtopics.pitfall: Geographic conventions can vary, so the framework in a question matters.
subtopics.mastery: Classify major land and water divisions using the stated convention.

subtopics.title: landmarks
subtopics.teaching: World landmarks represent ancient civilizations, architecture, religion, engineering or natural heritage.
subtopics.worked_example: The Great Wall of China is an extensive historic defensive structure associated with successive Chinese states and dynasties.
subtopics.pitfall: A modern national location does not identify the civilization or period of every part of a landmark.
subtopics.mastery: Connect famous landmarks with locations and broad significance.

subtopics.title: international organizations
subtopics.teaching: International organizations coordinate cooperation in areas such as peace, health, finance, education and development.
subtopics.worked_example: The United Nations provides a forum for international cooperation, while WHO focuses on international public health.
subtopics.pitfall: Organizations may overlap in interests but have different mandates.
subtopics.mastery: Match major organizations with their principal roles.

subtopics.title: world records
subtopics.teaching: Records describe exceptional measured achievements and require defined measurement criteria.
subtopics.worked_example: A record claim should specify what was measured, under what rules and over what period.
subtopics.pitfall: A viral claim is not a verified record merely because it is widely repeated.
subtopics.mastery: Evaluate record claims using definitions, measurements and authoritative evidence.

subtopics.title: Indian history
subtopics.teaching: Indian history includes ancient, medieval and modern periods with many regional kingdoms, empires, movements and political developments.
subtopics.worked_example: The Mauryan Empire, Gupta period, Delhi Sultanates, Mughal Empire and independence movement belong to different historical contexts.
subtopics.pitfall: Names from different periods should not be combined without chronology.
subtopics.mastery: Place major Indian developments in broad chronological order and identify significance.

subtopics.title: world history
subtopics.teaching: World history examines interactions among civilizations, states, economies, technologies and social movements.
subtopics.worked_example: The Industrial Revolution transformed production and urban life, while the two World Wars reshaped twentieth-century international politics.
subtopics.pitfall: Historical events should be understood in their time and context.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major world events, periods and broad consequences.

subtopics.title: civilizations
subtopics.teaching: Civilizations develop distinctive systems of settlement, governance, technology, writing, trade and culture.
subtopics.worked_example: The Indus Valley Civilization is known for planned urban settlements, drainage systems and evidence from Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
subtopics.pitfall: A civilization should be identified from multiple evidence types rather than one artifact.
subtopics.mastery: Connect major civilizations with characteristic achievements and evidence.

subtopics.title: arts and heritage
subtopics.teaching: Arts and heritage include architecture, sculpture, painting, music, dance, crafts, literature and traditions passed through generations.
subtopics.worked_example: Bharatanatyam and Kathak have distinct historical and performance traditions within Indian classical dance.
subtopics.pitfall: A modern performance inspired by a tradition is not necessarily identical to its historical form.
subtopics.mastery: Recognize major cultural forms and connect them with traditions or regions.

subtopics.title: important personalities
subtopics.teaching: Historical personalities are best understood through documented contributions, context and influence.
subtopics.worked_example: Mahatma Gandhi's leadership in India's freedom movement emphasized non-violent resistance and mass participation.
subtopics.pitfall: A personality can have multiple roles and interpretations across contexts.
subtopics.mastery: Identify important figures and accurately associate them with major contributions.

subtopics.title: physical features
subtopics.teaching: Physical geography studies natural features such as mountains, plateaus, plains, deserts, valleys and coastlines.
subtopics.worked_example: The Himalayas form a major mountain system in South Asia, while the Deccan Plateau covers much of peninsular India.
subtopics.pitfall: A plateau is elevated land with a relatively level surface, not simply another word for mountain.
subtopics.mastery: Classify major physical features and relate them to locations.

subtopics.title: climate
subtopics.teaching: Climate describes long-term atmospheric patterns, while weather describes short-term conditions.
subtopics.worked_example: Monsoon patterns strongly influence seasonal rainfall across much of South Asia.
subtopics.pitfall: One unusually rainy week does not define a region's climate.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish weather from climate and identify major climate influences.

subtopics.title: rivers and mountains
subtopics.teaching: Rivers and mountain systems shape landscapes, agriculture, settlement and transport.
subtopics.worked_example: The Ganga is a major river system of northern India, while the Himalayas form a major mountain barrier to the north.
subtopics.pitfall: A river's source, course and mouth are different geographic concepts.
subtopics.mastery: Locate major rivers and mountain ranges and describe basic relationships.

subtopics.title: maps
subtopics.teaching: Maps represent locations and spatial relationships using symbols, scale, directions and coordinates.
subtopics.worked_example: Map scale relates measured map distance to real-world distance.
subtopics.pitfall: Map symbols should be interpreted using the map legend.
subtopics.mastery: Use legends, scale, directions and coordinates to extract geographic information.

subtopics.title: human geography
subtopics.teaching: Human geography studies how people, settlements, economies and cultures interact with places and environments.
subtopics.worked_example: Population density compares people with the area they occupy and varies greatly between regions.
subtopics.pitfall: A large population does not necessarily mean high density if the area is also very large.
subtopics.mastery: Interpret basic population, settlement and human-environment patterns.

subtopics.title: everyday science
subtopics.teaching: Everyday science applies concepts from physics, chemistry and biology to familiar observations and processes.
subtopics.worked_example: A metal spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon in the same room because metal conducts heat away from the hand more readily.
subtopics.pitfall: A colder-feeling material is not necessarily at a lower temperature.
subtopics.mastery: Explain everyday observations using an appropriate scientific principle.

subtopics.title: space
subtopics.teaching: Space science studies objects and processes beyond Earth, including planets, stars, galaxies and their interactions.
subtopics.worked_example: Earth orbits the Sun, while the Moon orbits Earth; these motions help explain seasons and lunar phases.
subtopics.pitfall: The Sun is a star, not a planet.
subtopics.mastery: Identify major space objects and basic Earth-Sun-Moon relationships.

subtopics.title: inventions
subtopics.teaching: Inventions are designed solutions that introduce or apply ideas to solve practical problems; their development is often cumulative.
subtopics.worked_example: The printing press greatly expanded the ability to reproduce written material, building on earlier technologies and knowledge.
subtopics.pitfall: An invention rarely emerges entirely without earlier influences or related developments.
subtopics.mastery: Connect important inventions with their broad purpose and historical context.

subtopics.title: technology milestones
subtopics.teaching: Technology milestones are developments that significantly change how information, transportation, communication, health or production work.
subtopics.worked_example: The development of the internet transformed global digital communication and information exchange.
subtopics.pitfall: A milestone's importance should be judged by its impact rather than by being the newest technology.
subtopics.mastery: Recognize major technology developments and explain their broad significance.

subtopics.title: scientific personalities
subtopics.teaching: Scientific personalities are associated with documented discoveries, theories, experiments or contributions to scientific practice.
subtopics.worked_example: C. V. Raman's work on light scattering led to the discovery known as the Raman effect.
subtopics.pitfall: A person's fame does not establish that every claim attributed to them is accurate.
subtopics.mastery: Match major scientists with their verified contributions and fields.

subtopics.title: sports and rules
subtopics.teaching: Sports have defined rules governing scoring, equipment, player actions, boundaries and winning conditions.
subtopics.worked_example: In cricket, a batter's score, dismissals and innings structure follow specific laws rather than general ideas about team sports.
subtopics.pitfall: A rule from one sport cannot be assumed to apply to another.
subtopics.mastery: Identify the basic objective and distinctive rules of major sports.

subtopics.title: major tournaments
subtopics.teaching: Major tournaments bring teams or individuals together under defined competition formats, often representing national, club or professional levels.
subtopics.worked_example: The FIFA World Cup is an international football tournament involving national teams.
subtopics.pitfall: A tournament and a league use different competition structures and should not be treated as synonyms.
subtopics.mastery: Match major tournaments with their sports and broad format.

subtopics.title: sporting personalities
subtopics.teaching: Sporting personalities can be recognized for achievements, leadership or influence within their sport.
subtopics.worked_example: Sachin Tendulkar is associated with international cricket and represented India at the highest level.
subtopics.pitfall: A famous athlete's sport should not be inferred from popularity alone.
subtopics.mastery: Associate prominent athletes with their sports and documented achievements.

subtopics.title: records
subtopics.teaching: Sports records are measured achievements defined by a sport's rules, event category and record-keeping authority.
subtopics.worked_example: A world record in a 100-metre event is meaningful only when the event, rules and measurement conditions are specified.
subtopics.pitfall: A tournament victory and an individual record are different kinds of achievement.
subtopics.mastery: Distinguish records, titles, medals and match results and interpret record claims carefully.

subtopics.title: awards
subtopics.teaching: Sports awards recognize achievements such as outstanding performance, fair play, leadership or season-long excellence.
subtopics.worked_example: An award may be determined by a governing body, panel, voting process or competition-specific criteria.
subtopics.pitfall: Winning an award does not necessarily mean winning a tournament.
subtopics.mastery: Match notable sports awards with their broad purpose and recognize different award categories.

subtopics.title: major events
subtopics.teaching: Current awareness requires identifying significant recent events and understanding what happened, where, when and why it matters.
subtopics.worked_example: A strong event summary separates the confirmed event from speculation about possible future consequences.
subtopics.pitfall: Old information can appear current when reposted without its original date.
subtopics.mastery: Check publication date, event date and primary evidence before treating an event as current.

subtopics.title: public institutions
subtopics.teaching: Public institutions publish information, policies, reports and announcements that can be important sources for current affairs.
subtopics.worked_example: An official ministry or regulator may publish a notification that is more authoritative for a policy detail than an unverified social-media post.
subtopics.pitfall: An institution's official status does not mean every third-party interpretation of its notice is correct.
subtopics.mastery: Identify the responsible institution and distinguish its primary statement from commentary.

subtopics.title: science news
subtopics.teaching: Science news should connect a reported finding to the underlying study, evidence, limitations and date rather than relying only on a headline.
subtopics.worked_example: A study reporting an association between two factors does not automatically establish causation.
subtopics.pitfall: A headline may simplify or exaggerate the actual research conclusion.
subtopics.mastery: Read beyond headlines and identify what the evidence actually supports.

subtopics.title: sports news
subtopics.teaching: Sports news changes quickly, so current claims should be checked against recent schedules, results, official team or tournament sources and reliable reporting.
subtopics.worked_example: A transfer rumour is different from a confirmed signing, and a scheduled match is different from a completed result.
subtopics.pitfall: Old results can circulate again during later tournaments.
subtopics.mastery: Separate confirmed results, schedules, announcements and rumours.

subtopics.title: fact verification
subtopics.teaching: Fact verification checks a claim against reliable evidence, dates, original sources and independent confirmation when appropriate.
subtopics.worked_example: For a viral claim, trace it to the earliest credible source, check the date and compare it with authoritative evidence.
subtopics.pitfall: High engagement, screenshots and confident wording are not proof of truth.
subtopics.mastery: Apply a repeatable verification process before accepting or sharing a claim.

subtopics.title: classification
subtopics.teaching: Classification groups knowledge items by a shared defining property, category, origin, function or other rule.
subtopics.worked_example: India, Japan and Brazil can be grouped as countries, while Asia differs because it is a continent.
subtopics.pitfall: An item may belong to multiple categories, so the intended rule must be inferred from context.
subtopics.mastery: Identify the precise classification rule and apply it consistently.

subtopics.title: analogy
subtopics.teaching: An analogy compares a relationship between two items with a corresponding relationship in another pair.
subtopics.worked_example: 'India : New Delhi :: Japan : Tokyo' uses country-to-capital relationships.
subtopics.pitfall: Sharing a broad topic is not enough if the relationship itself differs.
subtopics.mastery: Identify the exact relationship and preserve its direction.

subtopics.title: sequences
subtopics.teaching: Sequences contain ordered items following a detectable rule involving numbers, letters, dates, categories or other information.
subtopics.worked_example: If a sequence progresses Monday, Wednesday, Friday, the rule advances by two days rather than simply listing weekdays.
subtopics.pitfall: A sequence may contain alternating or multiple rules, so test more than one step.
subtopics.mastery: Determine the simplest rule that explains all given transitions.

subtopics.title: odd one out
subtopics.teaching: Odd-one-out questions require identifying the item that does not follow the defining relationship shared by the others.
subtopics.worked_example: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Jupiter are planets, so an option naming the Moon would differ because it is a natural satellite.
subtopics.pitfall: An item can be 'different' in many ways, so the intended category matters.
subtopics.mastery: State the common rule for the majority before selecting the exception.

subtopics.title: mixed knowledge reasoning
subtopics.teaching: Mixed GK reasoning combines factual recall with comparison, classification, chronology and logical elimination.
subtopics.worked_example: If four options are historical figures and one is a scientific unit, both subject knowledge and category reasoning can identify the mismatch.
subtopics.pitfall: Pure guessing from familiarity is weaker than combining independent clues.
subtopics.mastery: Use factual knowledge first, then apply structured elimination and verify the final relationship.
